title: Resiliency scripting for partner comms and incident posture
content:
Purpose
This is a GTM-focused play/brief aimed at partner-facing comms and sales enablement when inference quality or availability degrades partially (not total outage). Goal: give partner reps, solutions engineers, and post-sale CS clear, short, and confidence-building scripts they can use in real time plus the competitive angles to emphasize.

High-level principles (keep these top-of-mind)
- Be surgical: default to two short facts (what happened, impact on customer) + one forward step (when/what we’re doing).
- Tiered transparency: more technical detail only if partner requests it. 
- Lead with mitigation, not blame: emphasize our fallbacks and continuity mechanisms.
- Signal predictability: share measurable SLOs and expected failover windows rather than vague promises.

Failure modes covered here (brief taxonomy)
- Localized model degradation: model variant serving issues (higher error-rate or hallucination for a subset of prompts).
- Regional capacity saturation: requests queued / elevated latency in a single region.
- Control-plane disruption: console/rollout visibility reduced while inference works.
- Storage/KV cache inconsistency: prefix cache misses cause transient cost and latency spikes.

What to surface to partners (concise checklist)
1) Scope: which org, route, model, and percentage of requests affected (approx).
2) Impact: latency delta, error-rate change, or quality regression (p50/p95/p99 if available).
3) Mitigation in flight: e.g., matrix routing to secondary region, revert rollout, swap to verified model variant, enable prefix cache bypass.
4) ETA / next update time: give a concrete window (e.g., 15–45m).
5) Ask: do you want us to proactively pause canary traffic, open a dedicated channel, or apply a temporary routing policy for you?

Short, skimmable scripts (pick based on audience)
- Developer/SRE (technical):
"We observed elevated p95 latency for route /v1/generate in us-west-2 affecting ~8% of requests. We're routing new requests to a secondary region and throttling burst queues; expected normalization in 20–30 minutes. If you need immediate consistency, we can pin your workspace to the secondary region now. I'll open a direct ticket and follow up with the trace links."

- Product Manager (partner PM):
"We detected partial capacity constraints in one region that may cause slower responses for some users. We're shifting requests to another region while we scale capacity; most traffic will return to normal within the next half hour. If you'd like, we can temporarily reduce max tokens for your key to keep costs predictable; do you want us to apply that?"

- Executive/Customer Success (non-technical):
"A subset of requests experienced slower performance for a short period. We've routed traffic through our backup region and are monitoring to make sure behavior returns to normal within 30 minutes. We’ll share a short incident summary and any customer-impact metrics once complete."

- Embedded legal/commercial prompt (for contractual asks):
"We are prioritizing a rapid operational fix; if this incident results in SLA credit eligibility, our CS lead will calculate credits per the contract and communicate next steps. For urgent contract questions, loop in your procurement/legal contact and we’ll coordinate."

Suggested internal sequence for partner-facing teams (recommended minimal steps)
1) Triage channel (CS + SE + incident commander) opens within 5m.
2) Initial customer note (short script) within 10m for impacted partners.
3) Apply temporary mitigations (route policy, model pin, token limit) as agreed.
4) Update every 30 minutes until resolved, then publish a short post-incident note with metrics and root-cause status.

Competitive deltas to highlight (how we sound vs others)
- We emphasize multi-region transparent routing as standard (vs vendors that only advertise single-region endpoints).
- We surface token-level cost impact and offer immediate temporary cost controls (billing transparency + token caps) — most competitors don't offer that at the moment.
- Our Console exposes per-route trace links and canary rollback history so partners can verify our remediation actions — call out the ability to "see what we did".
- For private deployments: we highlight air-gapped runbooks that allow customers to own final failover decisions (contrast with managed-only vendors).

Metrics to provide in comms (pick 2–3 for each update)
- Percentage of requests affected (est).
- p95 latency baseline vs current.
- Error rate delta (5xx or model-quality regression metric).
- Time-to-reroute (how long mitigation took).

Templates for short incident status updates (bullet style)
- Initial (10m): "Status: partial regional slow-down impacting ~8% of requests to model-x. Mitigation: routing to secondary region in progress. ETA next update: 20m. Contact: Jordan Kim (CS)"
- Mid (30m): "Status: traffic 90% rerouted, p95 back to +10% over baseline. Root-cause being investigated (capacity autoscaler + kernel mismatch). Next update: 60m."
- Resolution: "Status: resolved. Summary: brief description, measured impact, customer-facing mitigation, and next steps (rollback/patch/relax routing policy). Post-incident RCA to follow in 48–72h."

Operational knobs partners like to hear about
- Region pinning (guarantee all requests served from a chosen region).
- Model variant downgrade (fast switch to verified lower-latency variant).
- Token budget caps per API key during incidents.
- Silent-mode training: postpone async jobs that increase load.

Playbook for partner-enabled failovers (what SEs can do without infra)
1) Apply Workspace pin to target region in Console.
2) Select model variant toggle (documented rollback steps).
3) Enable token cap for customer key (Console / API).
4) Open dedicated support channel and send the short script.
(Include screenshots in the final guided-runbook doc)

Internal competitive notes (bullets for quick memorization)
- Major cloud AI endpoints: typically have global LB but lack token-cost transparency and per-route traceability.
- LLM API-first vendors: fast to acknowledge but often fall back to "we're investigating" with no per-token economics controls.
- Pure self-hosted runtimes: strong control but heavy ops lift; position Redwood as the middle ground (low ops + control features).

Confidence-building artifacts to offer partners post-incident
- Short incident summary with the three metrics above + timeline.
- Evidence of mitigation: Console trace link, rollback diff, and capacity scaling event logs sanitized for partner consumption.
- Commitment options: temporary dedicated routing, reserved pool, or private deploy checklist.

Open items / things to refine (actionable)
- [ ] Create a one-click Console flow for "partner emergency routing" (JIRA: ENG-PRIORITY-456).
- [ ] Build a partner-facing KB article with screenshots for region pinning.
- [ ] Define standard measurable thresholds for "affected percentage" estimation (SRE input).
- [ ] Draft legal-suggested wording for SLA credit notifications.

Notes to field reps (practical tips)
- Avoid technical detail overload — give one metric and one ask.
- If a partner asks for logs/traces, offer sanitized Console trace links rather than raw logs.
- Use the phrase "we routed traffic to our secondary region" instead of "we failed over" to reduce alarmism.

Appendix: quick comparator lines you can say in 1–2 sentences
- "Unlike general cloud endpoints, we expose per-route rollback history so you can independently verify remediation actions."
- "If you want full control during incidents, our Private offering gives you local runbooks with the same Console UX — we can walk you through the checklist."

Draft email template (post-incident, short)
"Subject: Incident summary — [short impact phrase] | Redwood Inference
Hi [Partner],
We experienced a partial regional capacity issue between [time1] and [time2] that affected an estimated [X%] of requests for [route / model]. We routed your traffic to a secondary region within [T] minutes; median latency returned to within [Y%] of baseline. Next steps: we’re publishing a short RCA in 48–72h and can discuss a dedicated routing or reserved pool if you’d like.
Thanks for your patience,
Jordan Kim — Partner CS"

Concluding note
This doc is intentionally concise and action-oriented. The next step is to convert the scripts into a two-slide cheat sheet for SEs + a one-click Console flow spec for ENG. Copy edits welcome — primary reviewer: Maya Patel (GTM).
